title: What is sampleV2 supposed to be? main.iter.md is still the scaffold stub
mainwork:
Write sampleV2's project head from the answer: set projectdescription in main.iter.md, replace the bracketed vision body with a real one (three to six sentences: what this project is, who it serves, the shape of the build), and create the first plan item for the structure the answer picked.

- main.iter.md frontmatter keys stay as scaffolded; only projectdescription changes.

- Do not create code nodes here — that is the plan item's job.

Agent-level details: files read — main.iter.md, .iter/config.iter.json, .iter/agents/{_shared,ingest,plan,code,testwriter,usecase}.md; `iter markers --project sampleV2` returns one node (the head) and an empty Orphanage.
question:
The request is "seed sampleV2 with its first code node so the build can
start", but main.iter.md still carries the scaffold placeholders: projectdescription
is "<one line on what this project is>" and the body is the bracketed vision stub.
Every agent context begins with that file, so whatever goes in it steers every
later work item — and nothing in the repository says what this project is.

What should sampleV2 be built as?

  A) A single-container CLI tool (one component, one test group to start)
     + Smallest thing that exercises the whole V2 structure end to end: one
       context node, one container, one component, real testgroups.
     + Matches how sampleV1 is shaped, so the two samples stay comparable.
     - Proves nothing about multi-container structure: no interface contracts
       between nodes, which is half of what structureV2 added.

  B) Two services with one interface contract between them
     + Exercises the part sampleV1 cannot: children.inputs / children.outputs,
       a real *.interface.iter.md, and the transport-neutral contract rules.
     + A use-case thread spanning both nodes becomes meaningful.
     - Roughly twice the scaffolding before the first green test.

  C) Leave it a bare harness: no product at all, just structure fixtures
     + Fastest, and structure tests do not need a plausible product.
     - Nothing to write real bizreqs or testgroups against, so the sample stops
       being a test of the engine and becomes a test of the file format only.

I recommend (B). The one thing sampleV1 cannot demonstrate after migration is an
interface contract carrying data between two code nodes, and that is exactly what
new users of the V2 structure get wrong. The extra scaffolding is one plan item.

title: Per-component test dirs or one top-level test/ for sampleV2?
mainwork:
Create sampleV2's first testgroup file in the layout the answer picked, with its shell scripts, and register the group in the owning code node's children.testgroups link.

- Between testwriter_min_tests_per_group (20) and max (100) assertions.
- Scripts must be deterministic and exit non-zero on any failed assertion.
- Finish with `iter runtests --project sampleV2 --group <label>` (neutral run).
question:
Before writing the first testgroup for sampleV2 I need to know where test
scripts live, and the two conventions in play disagree.

globalsettings.test_dir is "test", and _shared.md's parallelism example has a code
item on a component with codepath_ignore ["$ITER_TEST_DIR/"] while a testwriter item
owns <component>/test. That reads as: tests live INSIDE each component directory.
But sampleV1 (the migrated reference) keeps its scripts in a single top-level test/
directory shared across components. A greenfield project should not copy an accident.

Which layout does sampleV2 use?

  A) Per-component: <component>/test/*.testgroup.iter.md plus its scripts
     + The code/testwriter parallel-lock pattern in _shared.md works as written:
       two agents on one component at the same time, no lock conflict.
     + A component's testgroups link ({thisfiledir}/test/*.testgroup.iter.md)
       is the default in the code node template — zero configuration.
     - Test scripts are scattered; running "everything" means a walk, not a glob.

  B) Top-level test/ for the whole project, mirroring sampleV1
     + One place to look, one place to run from.
     - Breaks the codepath_ignore parallelism story: every testwriter item would
       lock the same top-level directory, serializing all test authoring.
     - Each node needs a hand-written testgroups link pointing out of its own
       directory, so the template default is wrong on every node.

I recommend (A), and I would treat sampleV1's shape as a V1 artifact rather than a
convention: the code node template's default testgroups link already assumes (A),
and (B) serializes work that the lock design goes out of its way to parallelize.

title: Name the greeting interface contract
mainwork: Create the interface contract file under interfaces/ with the id the answer picked. Fetch the skeleton first — `iter validate --project sampleV2 --file interfaces/<id>.interface.iter.md --template` — and fill it in; kind is request-reply. Then link it from both code nodes (children.outputs on the producer, children.inputs on the consumer).
question:
The greeting interface contract needs a name before the two code nodes can
link it as an input/output, and the id sticks: it is the filename, the node links,
and what every later agent greps for.

  A) greet-request  B) greeting-command  C) greet

I recommend (A): it names the message, not the verb or the component, which is what
the interface-contract standard asks for, and it leaves room for a second contract
(greet-reply) without renaming anything.
